methods.title: Frozen Memory and Matched Token Packing
methods.description: Full source histories are retained in a read-only single-layer bank, segmented losslessly into at most 256 pinned Qwen3 BPE tokens per turn segment. All selectors use the same source records, timestamps, metadata, memory wrapper and whole-item first-fit overflow policy under 512/1024/2048 tokens. This removes the pilot's extra file path formatting penalty. The controlled full-history bank is distinct from the legacy production Rail's 20-entry L1 capacity.

methods.title: Stronger Selectors and Isolated Controls
methods.description: Compare prefix, recency, lexical Jaccard, BM25 and existing hybrid. BM25 uses k1=1.2, b=0.75, positive idf. Remove only the weighted temporal contribution for selection ablation. Frequency is fixed at zero and importance at 0.5, so hybrid_no_time and Jaccard provide a sanity equivalence check. Representation changes only deterministic raw versus ACK exchange formatting in the adapted 20-item micro workload. Real EnhancedMemoryRail model-ACK acquisition is followed by canonicalization to exactly identical source records and solver prompts, isolating write-path overhead rather than learned extraction quality. No new algorithm or L2/L3 behavior is claimed.

methods.title: Repeated Real Agent Evaluation and Memory Reuse
methods.description: The 84-question stratified LongMemEval-S subset spans six question types plus abstention, with three actual solver calls per question/arm/budget and isolated conversation IDs. Full 500-history retrieval is separate from QA. Real DeepAgents use qwen-plus-2025-12-01, temperature zero, no tools, and one iteration. The pinned official task-specific grading prompts use qwen3-max-2026-01-23, with a second fixed-model audit and pending blinded human adjudication. Average repeats within each memory episode; stratified cluster bootstrap and paired cluster sign-flip tests with Holm correction. Eight synthetic banks each serve twenty distinct questions after a single build; actual query prefixes measure write amortization. Query wall time includes rate-gate waiting and excludes preprocessing; call latency and queue waiting are logged separately.

source_notes.memgpt: Verified arXiv abstract: virtual context management inspired by operating-system hierarchies moves information across memory tiers; demonstrations include document analysis and multi-session chat. Our fixed L1 Rail does not implement its autonomous virtual-memory controller.
source_notes.longmemeval: Verified author paper/repository: LongMemEval evaluates extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, updates and abstention, separating indexing, retrieval and reading. Our pinned cleaned S source is retained in full; QA is a fixed-hash balanced 84-question subset, while retrieval uses all 500 histories. Segmented records and a substituted Qwen judge are explicit deviations, not an official score.
source_notes.generative_agents: Verified arXiv abstract: natural-language experience records are synthesized into reflections and dynamically retrieved for planning behavior in an interactive simulation. This study neither implements reflection/planning nor tests social behavior; distinguish record retrieval from that broader architecture.
source_notes.lost_middle: Verified arXiv abstract: relevant information position affects multi-document QA and key-value retrieval in long contexts, with middle positions often harder. This motivates attention to information access but does not establish that our observed prefix truncation is caused by the same phenomenon.
source_notes.memorybank: Verified arXiv abstract: MemoryBank supports retrieval and updates for sustained personalized interaction, with forgetting and reinforcement influenced by elapsed time and importance. Our temporal ranking is a simple heuristic, not a replication of MemoryBank or its companionship evaluation.
source_notes.amem: Verified arXiv abstract: A-MEM creates structured notes and dynamically links and evolves memories, inspired by Zettelkasten organization. Our fixed lexical ranking lacks autonomous linking and evolution; no empirical comparison to A-MEM was run.

title: Evaluating Memory Retrieval: Evidence Quality and Lifecycle Cost
research_question: Under matched token budgets and controlled memory representations, how do selection and construction affect answer quality and lifecycle cost across repeated queries?

research_questions.title: Quality under Matched Budgets
research_questions.question: How does answer and evidence quality compare against stronger baselines with identical representations, formatting and token accounting?

research_questions.title: Attributing Component Effects
research_questions.question: Which differences remain when selection, representation and construction are varied separately?

research_questions.title: Lifecycle Cost under Memory Reuse
research_questions.question: How does measured write-plus-query cost change when a constructed memory serves multiple distinct queries?

writing_notes: Completed v2 experimental evidence is supplied, but human scoring review remains required. Do not claim a guaranteed reviewer-score improvement or scientific approval.
Use the general content renderer with the controlled_memory_eval_live adapter. Do not use the legacy jiuwenswarm_l1_v1 research profile's character-budget equations or diagrams.

Lead with the token-matched BM25 comparison, including negative or inconclusive differences. Pilot character-budget results belong in historical limitations, not as principal evidence of retrieval quality.

Fair-baselines and protocol-replication use the same 84 questions at different budgets; repeated calls and budgets are not independent tasks. Full 500-history retrieval is not 500-question answer accuracy.
Selection, representation and construction controls have different scopes. Representation/construction micro data cannot establish causal gains on the full-history workload.
Eight synthetic banks share templates. Reuse curves are measured distinct-query prefixes, not evidence for long-term natural memory generalization.
The production EnhancedMemoryRail still has 20 L1 entries. The frozen full-history bank does not demonstrate production persistence, multi-layer memory or team synchronization.

Figures and tables are generated from actual traced data. Report semantically judged accuracy, evidence-session hit definition, memory-cluster intervals and corrected tests without inventing algorithm novelty.

review_concerns.title: Weak Baseline and Budget Confounding
review_concerns.description: Match token accounting, representation and formatting; compare against stronger selectors before attributing gains to retrieval.

review_concerns.title: Construction, Representation and Selection Confounds
review_concerns.description: Change one component per ablation and preserve control traces; budget sensitivity alone is not a component ablation.

review_concerns.title: Unmeasured Memory Reuse
review_concerns.description: Measure multiple distinct queries against one built memory and count construction once.

review_concerns.title: Small Single-Run Sample and Scoring Limitations
review_concerns.description: Predeclare a broader evaluation, repeat runs, review scoring, account for dependence and verify benchmark protocol alignment.

review_concerns.title: Limited Algorithmic Novelty
review_concerns.description: Scope the contribution as a controlled and reproducible lifecycle-cost study. Better prose does not create a new retrieval algorithm, and these experiments do not guarantee acceptance.
